verdicts.note: Attacked for overstatement. The dossier has nothing that pulls toward pole_b: no treatment, diversion or non-police-response plank. Victim support and town halls are not prevention positions. Every safety item is enforcement: 'making excuses for criminals' (S1), 'criminals should be in jail and needles not in our parks' (S4), clearing more than 1,500 warrants and targeting drug dealers (S2, S4), and building strong cases with the prosecutor (S1). S1, S2 and S4 are in his frontmatter and support the claim. -2 high stands. Display check (no candidate-level _display row is allowed for candidate contests): office_does and race_blurb match _contest.md (an open seat; the 50.7% to 49.0% primary, S3; both candidates oppose SB 5974, which a judge temporarily halted, S5; Renzelman's 31 years, S1).

Attacked toward -1, since he is the sitting undersheriff and the outgoing sheriff sought a training variance for him (S5). The dossier records no endorsement from Hilderbrand, though. His full-time law-enforcement tenure is short: reserve service, an emergency hire about four years ago, undersheriff since July 2025 (S3, S5). His priorities are changes (issued rifles, in-house instructors, town halls; S2). Insider post against short tenure and change-oriented positions makes 0 a fair midpoint, and medium confidence matches that ambiguity. S1, S3 and S5 are in his frontmatter and support the basis. Display: the summary and all four highlights match the dossier (S2, S3, S4, S5, S9). Dossier concern: blake-richards.md says he has been a full-time Pullman firefighter-paramedic captain since 2007 (present tense, S3, S5) and also that he is the full-time undersheriff after full-time patrol work. The summary ('a full-time Pullman firefighter-paramedic captain') and the race blurb ('a Pullman fire captain') repeat the present-tense fire role. If he has left the Pullman job, both should switch to the past tense ('former'). The dossier cannot settle this.

Direction and magnitude hold. The dossier documents 31 years of full-time policing, more than 10 as chief (S1, S2), and endorsements from two former county sheriffs (S3). It is a proven-record pitch, but he is not the office's incumbent or its number two, so -1 rather than -2 is right. One defect: the basis quotes a slogan, 'Experience You Can Trust', that appears nowhere in the dossier. The score does not depend on it, but the quote should be dropped or sourced. S1, S2 and S3 are in his frontmatter. Display: the summary and highlights match the dossier: 11 years as Asotin chief, 13 years with Lewiston police and a deputy sergeancy (S2); the fentanyl quote (S1); jail treatment, education, job training and structured release (S1, S2); endorsements from former sheriffs Jeffers and Weber (S3).

Attacked both ways. Toward -2: he would 'aggressively confront the fentanyl epidemic through strong enforcement' and partner with the drug task force (S1, S2). Toward 0: he calls treatment and counseling critical, backs jail treatment, education, job training and structured release (S1, S2), runs on community policing (S1), and set up the Blue Bridge Alliance crisis-help fund (S5). The dossier records both halves explicitly, so a pole_a lean of -1 is well supported, and high confidence holds. S1, S2 and S5 are in his frontmatter. No missing scores proposed: Renzelman's line that he 'managed budgets responsibly' (S1) is a résumé claim, not a spending position, and _contest.md says neither candidate makes a spending pledge. Neither dossier has reform evidence.
